# Culture & Tech (컬처앤테크)

> Culture & Tech is a music studio in Seoul, South Korea. It produces original songs for live idols (credited "Produced By Sochan"), offers quality assurance and session services, and makes apps for musicians: Chord to MIDI and Storage Review. This site is the primary source for its works, contract terms, apps and contact details.

## Pages

- [Culture & Tech](https://cultureand.tech/): English homepage: services, apps for musicians, live-idol works, demo sets, contract information, FAQ, contact
- [컬처앤테크](https://cultureand.tech/ko/): Korean homepage with the same sections (라이브아이돌 오리지널곡 제작)
- [Chord to MIDI](https://cultureand.tech/apps/chord-to-midi/): the free web app that turns chord progressions into MIDI files and MIDI files back into chords (Korean: https://cultureand.tech/ko/apps/chord-to-midi/)
- [Storage Review](https://cultureand.tech/apps/storage-review/): the Mac storage cleaner whose default rules exclude music production files from removal (Korean: https://cultureand.tech/ko/apps/storage-review/)

## Live-idol original songs

- Recent works: (2026) Keep on lovin' me - KIPUERU; (2026) SE - KIPUERU; (2024) Oh My Sunshine - Utsuki (from ORIKA); (2024) NEK1 PR4DE SE (Opening Music)
- Deliverables: Full Mix, Instrumental, Stems (Drum, Bass, Synth, Lead, FX)
- Licences: Exclusive (only the group may use the song while it is active; converts to non-exclusive if the group disbands or suspends activities indefinitely) or Non-Exclusive (several teams may use the same song)
- Revisions: Non-exclusive 2 times, Exclusive 3 times (small audio tweaks only); lyrics adaptation does not count
- Scope: live (venue) performance; a digital release requires the credit "Produced By Sochan"
- Demo sets: https://soundcloud.com/sochan_life

## Apps for musicians

### Chord to MIDI

- What it does: type a chord progression, play it on a piano and download a standard MIDI file for any DAW or music app that imports MIDI files; open a MIDI file to get its harmony as a chord progression, spelled for the song's key (a chord chart, not a note-for-note transcription)
- Chord symbols: the spellings of real charts, from Cm7-5 and CΔ7 to C7(#9) and E7/G#; an unknown chord is reported by name, not guessed
- Where: https://chord-to-midi.app/ (Korean: https://chord-to-midi.app/ko/), in the browser, on computers and phones
- Price: every feature is free; no account is needed to type, play, download or import
- Privacy: progressions and MIDI files are processed on the device and never uploaded; the chord engine runs in the browser as WebAssembly
- Use: the progressions typed and the MIDI files made with it may be used in your own songs, commercial releases included

### Storage Review

- What it does: a macOS storage cleaner for musicians that finds caches, installers and leftovers worth removing and explains why each one is a candidate and whether it comes back
- Protection: music production files that match the default Music Production rules are excluded from removal. The rules recognize audio and stems; sample libraries and instruments (Kontakt, EXS, SFZ, SoundFont, REX); presets, patches, SysEx and MIDI files; DAW projects (Logic Pro, GarageBand, Cubase, Ableton Live, Pro Tools, FL Studio, Studio One, Bitwig Studio, Reaper); VST, VST3, Audio Unit, AAX and CLAP plug-ins and vendor content; music folders; including inside caches, downloads, package folders and build products. Protected items get no checkbox, and a folder holding protected content can't be removed as a whole. Video originals, device backups, credentials and AI assistant data are covered too
- Limits of the protection: inside a cache only ZIP-family archives are opened, so a cache holding another archive type (tar, gz, 7z, rar, dmg, pkg) is marked to review first and can still be selected by hand; formats and folder names the rules don't list aren't covered; a rule can be turned off (the app asks first)
- Safety: scanning only reads and nothing is selected by default; removals follow a fixed plan approved with Touch ID or the login password; each item is checked again right before removal; regular cleanup moves items to the Trash and a report shows what changed; deleting items already in the Trash is permanent, and the plan marks it that way
- Editions: Free (moves browser and app caches, installers and updaters and development caches to the Trash; can permanently delete items already in the Trash) and Expert, a one-time in-app purchase (more sources such as project environments, Xcode build caches, GitHub Actions runner leftovers, Final Cut Pro render files and duplicate files in iCloud Drive (Archive) folders; permanent deletion instead of the Trash for any item; a deeper scan; duplicate verification). The safety features are the same in both
- Privacy: files and scan results are processed on the Mac and not uploaded to the developer's servers; no analytics, no account; Apple handles Expert purchases and restores
- Requirements: macOS 14 or later
- Status: coming to the Mac App Store
